posts.content:
Around three and a half years ago, I started working with FedEx on autonomous trailer loading. I came from the enterprise AI world, and when I moved into physical AI and robotics at Dexterity, Inc., I had only a faint idea what I was signing up for.

I soon learned that loading 53-foot long-haul trailers is one of the hardest problems in physical AI. Every package is different. The environment is constantly changing. Exceptions are routine. The performance bar is unforgiving. And the system must perform safely and reliably, not in a lab, but inside mission critical, high volume hubs.

Solving that challenge required us to build more than a trailer-loading system. We had to create a few key foundational, general-purpose technologies, namely:
1. Foresight, a world model for manipulation that fuses vision, depth, and touch to understand its environment and reason many steps ahead.
2. Mech, a mobile dual-armed superhumanoid robot, built for industrial applications, and compact enough to fit inside a trailer.

Recently, FedEx announced the expansion of our trailer-loading product to it’s hub in Hagerstown, Maryland. This production expansion takes us beyond the initial site to a substantially larger operational scale.

In his recent Fortune interview, FedEx's CEO Raj Subramaniam described this work as "real physical AI" that just works. At FedEx Investor Day earlier this year, Kawal Preet, FedEx's EVP of planning, engineering and transformation, laid out the broader direction: scaling this technology across the US hubs in the next few years. And as our founder and CEO Samir Menon put it in the announcement, Hagerstown creates a blueprint for that network expansion.

I am grateful to the FedEx and Dexterity teams who have been partners throughout this journey. Thank you for the rigor, the patience, and for holding us to a standard that made the product better. 

Three and a half years ago, I had only a faint idea what I was signing up for.

I am very glad that I did.

On labor and efficiency, expect reduced injury exposure and staffing volatility in one of parcel's most physically demanding roles, plus more consistent throughput less prone to fatigue-driven slowdowns. For the broader market, framing this around hub-wide "physical AI" (destination planning, trailer assignment, maintenance) signals FedEx is chasing network-level orchestration gains, likely pressuring UPS and others to accelerate similar investments. Environmentally, tighter, more consistent loading could modestly cut linehaul trips per volume of freight, a real, if secondary, benefit behind the labor and reliability gains.

posts.content:
How do you know a world model is good?

That question gets lot less attention than the model themselves, but it is just as important. Real progress truly depends on evaluations you can trust.

Kevin Chavez, Founding Engineer at Dexterity, just published a new post on how we evaluate Foresight, Dexterity’s world model for manipulation, and the agents it powers in production.

What stands out is the rigor required to evaluate these systems well:
     - Real production distributions, not artificial sequences
     - Robustness to perception noise, not just idealized or isolated conditions
     - Evaluation of both planning quality and real-time execution
     - Real-time production telemetry from coordinated agent operations

The post also shows what that rigor enables in practice: predictive pipelining across two robot arms, 65.5% pipelining in production, and a net effective failure rate below 0.2%.

For world models, evals are not just scorekeeping. They determine whether the system is improving in ways that are measurable, repeatable, and verifiable.

That remains one of the less developed areas in Physical AI, especially at production scale. It is also one of the areas where Dexterity is defining the standard!

repost.content:
True force control, where intelligence and decision making is applied around contact, has never been deployed in production. Dexterity is the first.

Instinct, our force control agent doesn't just servo around force, or make small adjustments based on impedance or surface geometry properties. Many times, a robot has to back track, try something new, and remember why their previous movements did not achieve progress.

Imagine trying to solve a physical maze or puzzle while blindfolded, or feeling around the room at night, or even plugging in a good old USB-A cable (I swear those are 4 dimensional and break reality). You are building a map of the problem in your head, feeling around to gather information while also trying different solutions to the problem. As you keep going, your mental model gets closer and closer to the solution until you identify you've solved it.

Whether our robot is packing boxes into multiple a deep canyon of boxes surrounding by cliffs and edges, or trying to squeeze tires in between a rack, the robot has to reason about friction, neighboring objects and whether they are static or dynamic, the structure of the problem, and much more. 

Read more about it and why we think this is so novel in our blog post in the comments!

In production, robots get 600 watts in a 55°C truck. You struggle running 3x in these types of industrial environments, making it near impossible to force every decision—from simple motion to complex manipulation—through billions of parameters.

This is why we built a Transactable World Model for multi-agent coordination.

Specialized agents. Shared world state. Real-time consistency. Optimized for the constraints of operating in the real world.

Rather than one monolithic model trying to do everything and overheating, we use multiple agents transacting against reality as it actually exists.

Watch our Founding Engineer Robert Sun break down why this architecture matters when Physical AI leaves the lab. Full presentation in the comments ↓

We're excited to announce Foresight  — a world model built for the physical world!

Most world models observe. Foresight acts. It's a real-time, physics-consistent representation of the physical world that enables robots to perceive, reason, and manipulate objects at production speed, not in simulation, but in real industrial environments. It's a production system trained with experience from over 100 million autonomous actions, and it's advancing every day.

In autonomous truck loading, Foresight powers our dual-armed robot, Mech, with a 4D packing agent that reasons across three spatial dimensions plus time. Foresight evaluates every option in under 400 milliseconds, jointly optimizing density, stability, reachability, and dual-arm coordination, while predicting how each placement affects the integrity of the entire truck.

Foresight is application-agnostic and hardware-agnostic: it runs across six applications, four robot types, and five hand types. Its agentic architecture is safety-first and interpretable - operators can see exactly why the system makes each decision.

Physical AI is not a future promise; it is a system that perceives, decides, and acts in the real world, right now.

posts.content:
The announcement of FedEx and Dexterity, Inc. expanding robotics trailer loading to the Hagerstown Hub is an exciting milestone—and one I’m incredibly proud because enterprise-scale deployment of Physical AI is fundamentally different from scaling digital AI.

While software can often be deployed with the push of a button, Physical AI must reliably operate in the real world, where every decision interacts with people, equipment, facilities, and constantly changing environments. Getting from an impressive demo to production at enterprise scale requires years of disciplined engineering and operational excellence.

True production readiness demands capabilities well beyond AI models:

* Product & Functional Safety
* Validation & Verification
* Component Selection & Qualification
* Reliability Growth Modeling & Testing
* Supply Chain Development & Execution
* Inbound & Outbound Logistics Integration
* Manufacturing Planning & Certification
* Parts, Service & Maintenance Readiness
* Operator Training & Site Readiness

This is why scaling Physical AI is so challenging—and why so few companies have successfully crossed the gap from lab demonstrations to sustained production deployments.

Congratulations to Samir Menon and the entire Dexterity team, and to Stephanie C. and FedEx team, on this achievement. This milestone reflects years of collaboration, relentless innovation, rigorous testing, and a shared commitment to operational excellence.

I’m excited to see what comes next as Physical AI continues its journey from promising technology to enterprise-scale reality.

Robert Sun Mukesh R. Steven Schwartzberg

posts.content:
We're excited to announce Foresight  — a world model built for the physical world!

Most world models observe. Foresight acts. It's a real-time, physics-consistent representation of the physical world that enables robots to perceive, reason, and manipulate objects at production speed, not in simulation, but in real industrial environments. It's a production system trained with experience from over 100 million autonomous actions, and it's advancing every day.

In autonomous truck loading, Foresight powers our dual-armed robot, Mech, with a 4D packing agent that reasons across three spatial dimensions plus time. Foresight evaluates every option in under 400 milliseconds, jointly optimizing density, stability, reachability, and dual-arm coordination, while predicting how each placement affects the integrity of the entire truck.

Foresight is application-agnostic and hardware-agnostic: it runs across six applications, four robot types, and five hand types. Its agentic architecture is safety-first and interpretable - operators can see exactly why the system makes each decision.

Physical AI is not a future promise; it is a system that perceives, decides, and acts in the real world, right now. 

Think you can pack a truck better than a robot?

How do you know a world model is good?

That question gets lot less attention than the model themselves, but it is just as important. Real progress truly depends on evaluations you can trust.

Kevin Chavez, Founding Engineer at Dexterity, just published a new post on how we evaluate Foresight, Dexterity’s world model for manipulation, and the agents it powers in production.

What stands out is the rigor required to evaluate these systems well:
     - Real production distributions, not artificial sequences
     - Robustness to perception noise, not just idealized or isolated conditions
     - Evaluation of both planning quality and real-time execution
     - Real-time production telemetry from coordinated agent operations

The post also shows what that rigor enables in practice: predictive pipelining across two robot arms, 65.5% pipelining in production, and a net effective failure rate below 0.2%.

For world models, evals are not just scorekeeping. They determine whether the system is improving in ways that are measurable, repeatable, and verifiable.

That remains one of the less developed areas in Physical AI, especially at production scale. It is also one of the areas where Dexterity is defining the standard!

article.linkLabel: Open article: Inside Foresight: From Packing Evaluation to Real-Time Coordination by dexterity.ai

posts.content:
We've been investing in physical AI since 2017. We've seen a lot of teams try to bring intelligence into the physical world.

One company has consistently operated on a different plane: Dexterity, Inc..

Most world models are built for observation — video generation, game simulation. They have no concept of contact. They cannot predict what happens when a gripper touches a box, or whether a stack of 40 will hold when the 41st is placed incorrectly.

Foresight is a different class of model. Built for manipulation, not observation. Trained on 100M+ autonomous actions in real production facilities. Zero safety incidents. Every placement decision in under 400ms.

Behind it: Robert Sun at the bleeding edge of physical systems. Kevin Chavez building the reasoning core. Ben Varkey Benjamin laying the perception foundation. And Samir Menon's conviction since day one — build systems that are safe, reliable, and production-grade from the start.

The gap between world models built in research and world models forged in production will define the next era of automation.

Dexterity, Inc. didn't wait for the category to form. They built it.

posts.content:
Foresight, our world model, is built from over 100 million autonomous actions in production and designed for manipulation, not just observation. Every robot action changes the physical world, so the system must adapt in real time, reasoning about object geometry, contact dynamics, weight distribution, stability, and more, before every action. Every decision is fully interpretable and safe.

NVIDIA’s technology helped unlock its full potential. Our engineering team redesigned Foresight’s perception pipeline using NVIDIA technology. The biggest gain was not just speed, but data utilization. Previous versions of Foresight were forced to throw away most of what the sensors could see. On NVIDIA GPUs, Foresight now sees everything.

The results:

 • 17x faster perception from 1,508ms to 90ms per cycle
 • 32x more sensor data processed per cycle
 • Decision cycles below 400ms in complex applications like truck loading

Thank you to the NVIDIA team for the support, the technology, and for recognizing Dexterity at #GTC2026 as an upcoming Physical AI pioneer bringing robotics into the real world. We’re excited to keep building on this partnership.

- NVIDIA named Dexterity, Inc. among the upcoming Physical AI pioneers taking robotics to the real world at NVIDIA GTC 2026. Shout out to Sumay Parikh; you rock!

- At FedEx's Investor Day in Memphis, FedEx and Dexterity showcased Foresight running on our super-humanoid robot Mech to 100s of public market investors. FedEx shared their vision to scale trailer loading and unloading across thousands of dock doors across 20 US hubs over the next few years. Really grateful for the FedEx collaboration Kawal Preet, O.P. Skaaksrud, Stephanie C., and Steven Schwartzberg.

- Next week, we're opening Foresight to the research/student community with the Foresight API Challenge. $50,000 in prizes. Build a packing agent leveraging our Foresight truck loading arena and compete on a public leaderboard.

Keep an eye out for Kevin Chavez’s upcoming post on our production-grade evaluation results, and Robert Sun's deep dive into our perception pipeline.
